answer.rationale: The low-cost vendor's quote meets the 18% cut on its own, and the primary-supply contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew. Memory_c2 records that the same low-cost vendor delivered quick onboarding and accurate invoicing last year; pulling the archive confirms whether that record still holds. Memory_c3 adds that the constrained component already has a second source, so switching the primary does not re-introduce a single point of failure for the bottleneck part. Given the assembly line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, any disruption would bite immediately; this favors reusing a vendor whose performance is already documented rather than experimenting with a new one. The alternatives are weaker in this cycle: renewing the incumbent does not meet the 18% cut alone; renegotiating takes time we do not have before day 85 expiry; adding a second source adds cost rather than reducing it; deferring lets the contract lapse with no fallback in place. I am preserving optionality by keeping the incumbent relationship warm for the next cycle in case volume or delivery risk changes, but the single decision this cycle goes to switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor.
